What these measurements do and do not establish

IoU measures area overlap with the development references. A .90 threshold exposes border differences that .50 matching can hide. A failed .90 match can represent a misplaced border on a detected panel; it does not necessarily mean a missing module. Corner RMSE uses matched reference quadrilaterals and is measured in source pixels. Width and height CV describe variation inside fitted groups in the image plane; perspective can create legitimate variation. A regular grid can still be consistently misplaced.

The six labeled examples are development samples with unknown training overlap. They do not establish performance on unseen sites. Partial image-edge panels and unsupported fits retain their observed outline. Layout fitting does not add a panel solely because a grid position exists. The external orthomosaic has no reference labels, so no precision, recall, false-positive count or missed-panel count is asserted.

Controlled input-resolution check

Development image640 input: IoU ≥ .90 matches1280 input: IoU ≥ .90 matches

These are detector-input settings on the same source images, not new capture resolution. Larger model inputs are not uniformly better; flight GSD, model training scale, source blur and module size still matter.

Research decision

Shared shape is the current best compromise on the default RGB example: it reduces variation while retaining observed centers. A stronger table grid and image-edge refinement need more work because cleaner geometry can reduce strict overlap agreement. The practical engine should combine a trained module detector with table context, source-supported geometry and an auditable fallback. A commercial panel inventory can also supply persistent geometry that is registered to each survey.

External-site orientation probe

Inspection suggests better coverage in parts of the rotated outputs and fewer large background boxes in inspected areas. Errors remain, and rotation also changes tile placement: this probe cannot isolate orientation from tiling or establish an accuracy gain. All outlines are mapped back to the same original image coordinates. Panel IDs are temporary within each run and do not identify the same module across different input rotations. More observations do not establish a correct module inventory, and neither rotation is selected as a winner by its count.

Opus 5.5 consultation

A completed read-only consultation reported claude-opus-5-5. Its advice was to fit geometry across neighboring panels, separate panel presence from panel shape, and verify physical outer-frame evidence before shifting borders. This was advice, not independent validation.

The experiments test those recommendations. Stronger grid constraints and gradient refinement were rejected as the default because they reduced strict overlap agreement on RGB 0031. The controlled input study also found that larger detector inputs are not uniformly better. Shared shape remains an experimental compromise with explicit fallbacks.
